headline: A rough night on Wall St dragged most of your portfolio lower, with PLS taking the biggest hit today as lithium sentiment stays sour and oil's sharp drop weighed on FUEL.

movers.name: Pilbara Minerals
movers.note: PLS had a tough session today, dropping 3.75% to $5.91. Lithium sentiment remains deeply divided — analysts are split on whether prices have bottomed or have further to fall. The broader ASX mining sector was in the red today, with lithium and gold stocks sliding across the board.

movers.name: Global X AI ETF
movers.note: The AI ETF slipped 1.74% today to $18.05. It tracks global AI-related stocks, so last night's sharp NASDAQ fall (down 3%) is feeding through — when US tech sneezes, this ETF catches a cold.

movers.name: Microsoft
movers.note: Microsoft dropped 2% last night to $419.44. No specific breaking bad news — it was caught in a broad NASDAQ sell-off. The stock is still underwater in your portfolio at -5.3% overall.

movers.name: Take-Two Interactive
movers.note: Take-Two slipped about 1% last night to $214.42, largely carried down by the wider tech and gaming sector sell-off on the NASDAQ. Still down 7.5% overall in your portfolio.

movers.name: Vanguard Emerging Markets ETF
movers.note: VGE fell 0.94% today to $92.03. Emerging markets got hit by the weaker Australian dollar (which fell 1.15% against the USD) and broader risk-off sentiment flowing from the US.

movers.name: BetaShares Global Energy ETF
movers.note: FUEL dipped 0.8% today to $8.70. Crude oil (WTI) dropped sharply last night — down 3.35% to $89.92 a barrel — as OPEC cut its demand forecast for 2026, meaning they now expect the world to need less oil than previously thought. Less demand = lower prices = weaker energy stocks.

movers.name: Alphabet (Google)
movers.note: Google edged down 0.69% last night to $366.74, a relatively small move in what was a rough night for the broader NASDAQ. No specific company news — general tech sector pressure. Still up 26.9% overall in your portfolio, the strongest performer.

movers.name: Vanguard US Total Market ETF
movers.note: VTS nudged up 0.31% today to $521.82, a solid result given it tracks US stocks — the ASX-listed version can move slightly differently to the underlying US market due to currency and timing effects. Small but positive.

movers.name: Vanguard Diversified High Growth ETF
movers.note: VDHG was essentially flat today, edging up 0.12% to $75.95. Its diversification across asset classes is doing its job — cushioning the blow when individual sectors sell off hard.

watch_today.title: PLS.AX — Lithium pain continues
watch_today.detail: Pilbara dropped 3.75% today and is now down 12.3% overall in your portfolio. The lithium market remains deeply split — some analysts think prices have bottomed, others see more downside. No clear catalyst to buy more right now. Hold and watch for any signs of lithium price stabilisation.

watch_today.title: MSFT — NASDAQ sell-off hit hard last night
watch_today.detail: Microsoft fell 2% last night as the NASDAQ dropped 3%. It's your second-largest holding by value and is already 5.3% underwater. No fundamental bad news, just broad market pressure. No reason to sell, but worth watching if the US sell-off continues tonight.

watch_today.title: GXAI.AX — AI ETF sliding with the NASDAQ
watch_today.detail: GXAI fell 1.74% today and is down 5.15% overall. It mirrors global AI stocks, so when the NASDAQ falls 3% (as it did last night), this follows. If you believe in the long-term AI theme, this dip isn't alarming — but watch tonight's US open for further direction.

watch_today.title: FUEL.AX — Oil's big drop worth watching
watch_today.detail: Crude oil fell 3.35% last night to $89.92 a barrel after OPEC cut its 2026 demand forecast. FUEL dropped 0.8% today in response. If oil keeps sliding, expect more pressure on this ETF. It's still slightly in the green overall (+2.86%), but the trend bears watching this week.

watch_today.title: US markets open tonight — brace for volatility
watch_today.detail: The S&P 500 fell 1.84% and the NASDAQ dropped 3% last night. Gold also sold off sharply (-2.83%) and the Aussie dollar fell 1.15% against the USD to 70.5 cents. Risk-off sentiment (investors pulling back from riskier assets) is building. Tonight's US open will be key — if selling continues, your US holdings (GOOG, MSFT, TTWO) will feel it.

watch_today.title: Labor's tax legislation passes the lower house
watch_today.detail: The Albanese government's new tax laws have passed the House of Representatives despite questions about constitutional validity. If it clears the Senate, changes could affect investors through modifications to tax policy. Worth keeping an eye on as it moves to the Senate.

markets.summary: Last night was ugly on Wall Street. The NASDAQ shed 3% and the S&P 500 fell 1.84%, dragged down by broad tech selling. Gold dropped nearly 3% and oil fell over 3% after OPEC trimmed its demand outlook — meaning they expect global oil consumption to be lower than previously forecast. The Aussie dollar also weakened, falling 1.15% to around 70.5 US cents, which means your US-denominated holdings are worth slightly less in AUD terms. ASX 200 data wasn't available at close today.

indicators.note: Broad US sell-off last night — tech led the losses

indicators.note: OPEC cut 2026 demand forecast — less expected consumption = lower prices

politics.summary: Federal budget debt is front and centre this week, with Treasurer Jim Chalmers defending a projected $53-54 billion debt burden. Meanwhile, Labor's new tax legislation has passed the lower house despite legal questions, and the PM is standing firm on the reforms.

stories.title: 'Not a lot': Chalmers defends $53 billion debt burden
stories.why_it_matters: Treasurer Jim Chalmers is defending the federal budget's projected debt of around $53-54 billion, calling it 'not a lot' in the context of the overall economy. South Australia has reportedly taken a subtle dig at Chalmers over the figures. For investors, high government debt can eventually put upward pressure on interest rates or lead to spending cuts — worth keeping in the back of your mind.

stories.title: Labor's tax legislation passes the lower house amid constitutional questions
stories.why_it_matters: Labor's new tax legislation has cleared the House of Representatives. Sky News host Sharri Markson and others are raising concerns it may be constitutionally invalid — meaning it could face a legal challenge before it ever takes effect. Labor has also rejected calls to address bracket creep (where inflation pushes workers into higher tax brackets without a real pay rise). The bill now heads to the Senate.

stories.title: Albanese digs in on tax reforms, says they're good for 'democracy and social cohesion'
stories.why_it_matters: Prime Minister Albanese is standing firm on the government's tax reform package, framing it as being about fairness and social cohesion rather than just fiscal policy. He's not backing down despite political pressure and legal questions. This signals the government intends to push the legislation through the Senate, so it's likely to remain a hot political topic over the coming weeks.

stories.title: SA takes a dig at Chalmers as budget heads for record $54b debt
stories.why_it_matters: The AFR reports South Australia has taken a swipe at Treasurer Chalmers as the federal budget tracks toward a record $54 billion debt. The inter-government tension adds political noise to what's already a difficult budget environment. A growing debt pile can mean less fiscal flexibility for future governments — relevant if you're thinking about the longer-term economic backdrop.

ai.summary: The big AI story today is a rare show of unity: the CEOs of OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, and Microsoft have jointly called for a law requiring DNA screening to prevent synthetic biology being weaponised. Separately, AI regulation is under fire from multiple angles — the UN, the Archbishop of Canterbury, and a new US bipartisan bill are all pushing for tougher rules.

stories.title: OpenAI, Anthropic, Google & Microsoft CEOs call for DNA screening law
stories.why_it_matters: The heads of the world's top AI labs — OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, and Microsoft — have co-signed an open letter calling for laws requiring DNA screening of synthetic biology orders. Their argument: in an era where AI can teach almost anyone how to create dangerous pathogens, synthetic DNA and RNA that could be repurposed for biological weapons is too easy to order online. It's a striking moment of cross-industry agreement on a safety issue, and signals AI companies are increasingly aware their technology has dual-use risks beyond just disinformation.

stories.title: GPT-5.5 dominates $1,500 LLM hacking test while Gemini refuses to even try
stories.why_it_matters: In a $1,500 AI benchmark test focused on security (essentially testing how well AI models can find and exploit vulnerabilities — a common use in cybersecurity), OpenAI's GPT-5.5 came out on top. Meanwhile, Google's Gemini reportedly refused to even attempt the task. This matters for your GOOG holding: if Gemini keeps being seen as overly cautious or less capable than GPT-5.5 in competitive benchmarks, it could weigh on Google's AI credibility with enterprise customers.

stories.title: UN calls for AI regulation as environmental footprint grows
stories.why_it_matters: The United Nations is calling for stronger global AI regulation, citing the growing environmental cost of running AI systems at scale — think massive data centres consuming huge amounts of electricity and water. The UN wants international rules, not just country-by-country approaches. For investors in AI-related stocks or ETFs like GXAI.AX, increased regulation could slow adoption or raise operating costs for AI companies.

stories.title: A bipartisan US bill on AI takes shape in Washington
stories.why_it_matters: A rare bipartisan (both Democrat and Republican) AI regulation bill is being discussed in Washington DC. Getting politicians from both sides of the aisle to agree on tech regulation is genuinely unusual. The details aren't fully public yet, but any US federal AI law would have major implications for how companies like Google and Microsoft build and deploy their AI products — and could reshape the competitive landscape.

stories.title: Archbishop of Canterbury tells Parliament AI rules fail to protect human dignity
stories.why_it_matters: The Archbishop of Canterbury has told the UK Parliament that current AI regulations are 'inadequate' and fail to protect human dignity. He's calling for rules that go beyond just economic and safety concerns to include ethical and social dimensions. It's a sign that AI governance is moving beyond tech circles into mainstream moral and political debate — the kind of pressure that often precedes real regulatory change.

sport.summary: Big NRL Round 14 action underway — the Storm survived a thriller against the Knights, the Roosters smashed the Raiders, and there's a huge Storm injury blow. In AFL, Adelaide captain Jordan Dawson is generating emotional support after some news this week. Wimbledon prep is heating up in tennis.

stories.title: Storm survive 62-point thriller vs Knights but lose star for the season
stories.why_it_matters: Melbourne Storm edged the Newcastle Knights 32–30 in a wild 62-point game at AAMI Park tonight. The drama was off the field too — a Storm superstar has been ruled out for the season after being sent to hospital during the match. This is a significant blow to Melbourne's premiership hopes for the second half of the season.

stories.title: Roosters demolish Raiders 26–0, with DCE and Walker starring in Blues audition
stories.why_it_matters: The Sydney Roosters put on a clinic against the Canberra Raiders tonight, winning 26–0 at GIO Stadium. According to Fox Sports, winger performances and contributions from Nathan Cleary's rival halfbacks including Daly Cherry-Evans (DCE) and Adam Walker served as strong State of Origin auditions — with Blues selection pressure building ahead of the series.

stories.title: AFL rallies around 'superhuman' Adelaide captain Jordan Dawson
stories.why_it_matters: The AFL world has rallied around Adelaide Crows captain Jordan Dawson following emotional scenes this week. Dawson, described as 'superhuman' by teammates and opponents alike, has drawn an outpouring of support from across the football community. Teammate Isaac Cumming also revealed his top five AFL players, with Dawson making a strong impression on those around him.

stories.title: Broncos halfback succession plan hit by major contract twist
stories.why_it_matters: There's a contract drama brewing at the Brisbane Broncos around their halfback succession plan — the club's strategy to replace their current playmaker has hit an unexpected twist, putting 'shock heat' on several squad members according to Fox Sports' whispers column. With the Broncos hosting the Titans at Suncorp tomorrow night, the timing adds extra intrigue to what's already a Queensland derby.
